gene_name: transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily M member 2

gene_function: Renal vasopressin receptor coupled to Gs and cAMP rather than to calcium, governing water reabsorption. Included as a within-family specificity control: a genuine social effect should NOT appear here.

Encodes the oxytocin prepropeptide made in hypothalamic magnocellular neurons and cleaved to the nine-amino-acid hormone. Its promoter and intron 1 CpGs are studied as the supply-side counterpart to OXTR methylation, though peripheral expression is low.
Neuronal nitric oxide synthase, activated by the calcium-calmodulin complex and producing the gaseous messenger that feeds back on oxytocin release. Couples CICR output to retrograde signalling.

Skeletal-muscle-type ryanodine receptor, the calcium release channel opened by cADPR downstream of CD38. Calcium released through it opens neighbouring RyR channels, making this a positive feedback loop in the strict sense: calcium triggering further calcium release.

Vasopressin precursor, co-released with oxytocin and acting on partly overlapping receptors, generally with opposite valence for social vigilance. Its methylation is a classic readout of early-life stress in maternal separation models.

SERCA2 pump, returning cytosolic calcium to the ER and refilling the store. Refill is what stops the positive feedback loop running to exhaustion, making oxytocin signalling oscillatory rather than a single decaying surge.

gene_name: calcium voltage-gated channel subunit alpha1 C
gene_function: L-type voltage-gated calcium channel Cav1.2, whose depolarisation-driven calcium entry can itself ignite the RyR positive feedback loop. Also one of the most robust cross-disorder psychiatric GWAS loci.

The Gq-coupled oxytocin receptor; activation drives PLC to IP3 and ignites the calcium-induced calcium release positive feedback loop. Its MT2 region, especially the CpG at -934, is the most replicated methylation target in social behaviour research.

gene_name: calcium/calmodulin dependent protein kinase II alpha
gene_function: Calcium/calmodulin kinase II alpha, the main decoder of calcium transients into lasting synaptic change through autophosphorylation. Where a calcium signal becomes a durable behavioural trace.

Ectoenzyme generating cyclic ADP-ribose, the messenger that opens ryanodine receptors and so switches on the CICR positive feedback loop; it is required for hypothalamic oxytocin release. Cd38 knockout mice show social amnesia that oxytocin rescues.

Type 3 IP3 receptor, biased towards initiating rather than sustaining calcium waves, so it governs how readily the loop starts. Completes the IP3 receptor trio feeding the CICR positive feedback loop.

Imprinted, paternally expressed gene whose loss reduces hypothalamic oxytocin production; mutations cause Schaaf-Yang syndrome with autistic features. Sits at the intersection of the oxytocin system and the imprinted-DMR literature.
SERCA3, a lower-affinity pump expressed in non-muscle and immune cells, providing store refill in the tissues sampled in saliva and blood. The peripherally relevant SERCA isoform.

gene_name: calcium voltage-gated channel subunit alpha1 D
gene_function: Cav1.3 L-type channel, activating at more negative voltages and supporting pacemaking and tonic calcium influx. Complements CACNA1C in linking excitability to the calcium loop.
FKBP12.6, the higher-affinity RYR2 stabiliser whose loss produces leaky channels and dysregulated release. The gating counterpart to FKBP1A in cardiac and neuronal tissue.
Type 1 IP3 receptor, releasing endoplasmic reticulum calcium in response to the IP3 generated by OXTR, Gq and PLC. It provides the initial spark that the RyR positive feedback loop then amplifies.

Cardiac-type ryanodine receptor, also widely expressed in brain, where it sustains the calcium positive feedback loop underlying transmitter release and plasticity. One of the RyR family implicated in oxytocin signalling in Ein-Dor et al. (2024, Communications Psychology).

Two-pore channel releasing calcium from acidic lysosomal stores in response to NAADP, a second messenger also generated by CD38. Represents the lysosomal, non-ER limb of oxytocin-triggered calcium signalling.
The lysosome-restricted two-pore channel and principal NAADP target, triggering local calcium that primes ER release. Links CD38 enzymatic output to the CICR loop by a route independent of cADPR.
Aspartate beta-hydroxylase, whose junctin isoform completes the calsequestrin-triadin-RyR complex that regulates store-dependent gating. Represents the luminal regulatory arm of the loop.
CD38 paralogue, also called CD157, with the same ADP-ribosyl cyclase activity and partly redundant cADPR supply to the CICR loop. Studied in social anxiety and in Parkinson disease.
Second of three genes encoding identical calmodulin protein, differing only in regulatory sequence and hence in methylation-sensitive expression. Dosage, not sequence, is what varies here.
Immunophilin FKBP12, binding ryanodine and IP3 receptors and stabilising them closed to prevent calcium leak. Its methylation bears on how tightly the CICR loop is clamped between signals.
G11 alpha subunit, functionally near-identical to GNAQ and largely redundant with it. Included so the transducer step is not represented by a single gene.

The principal brain vasopressin receptor, Gq-coupled like OXTR and feeding the same IP3 and RyR calcium loop. Promoter methylation and the linked RS3 repeat are studied for pair bonding, social recognition and aggression.
Calmodulin, the universal calcium sensor that activates CaMKII and directly modulates RyR and IP3 receptor gating. Three genes encode an identical protein, so coverage across all three matters.
Third calmodulin gene; total calmodulin availability is the sum of CALM1 to CALM3, making the trio a natural test of dosage-sensitive methylation effects.

gene_name: calcium/calmodulin dependent protein kinase II delta
gene_function: CaMKII delta, the isoform dominant outside neurons and therefore the one measurable where the tissue is saliva or blood. The peripherally accessible member of the family.
Calsequestrin 1, the high-capacity luminal calcium buffer that sets how much calcium is available for RyR to release. Determines the size of the releasable store.
Type 2 IP3 receptor, higher affinity for IP3 than ITPR1 and dominant in secretory and glial cells. Sets how small an oxytocin signal needs to be to ignite the positive feedback loop.
The store-operated calcium entry channel opened by STIM1, replenishing ER calcium after release. Completes the refill circuit that sustains pulsatile signalling.
Phospholipase C beta 1, the Gq effector hydrolysing PIP2 to IP3 and DAG immediately downstream of OXTR and AVPR1A. The first amplification step in the pathway.

The brain-enriched ryanodine receptor and the main amplifier of the CICR positive feedback loop in neurons. Methylation here indexes loop gain, meaning how much a given oxytocin signal is amplified, rather than receptor availability.
ER calcium sensor detecting store depletion and migrating to the membrane to open ORAI1. The trigger for store-operated entry, without which repeated oxytocin signalling would exhaust the store.

Triadin, the anchoring protein coupling calsequestrin to the ryanodine receptor so that luminal calcium load is sensed by the channel. Structural rather than signalling, but rate-limiting for release.

Proopiomelanocortin, the pituitary precursor cleaved to ACTH and also the shared precursor of beta-endorphin and MSH. Its methylation links the HPA axis to the opioid and appetite systems.

REDD1, a glucocorticoid-induced inhibitor of mTOR signalling, linking stress hormones to suppressed protein synthesis and plasticity. A plausible route from chronic cortisol to reduced neural remodelling.

Regenerates active cortisol from inert cortisone within target tissues, so local exposure can exceed circulating levels. Explains why tissue glucocorticoid action is not readable from serum cortisol alone.

Prohormone convertase 2, directing POMC processing towards alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin rather than ACTH. Determines which branch of the precursor's output predominates.
Urocortin 3, the most CRHR2-selective ligand, implicated in terminating the stress response and in social behaviour. The clearest molecular handle on stress offset rather than onset.
Annexin A1, mediating the rapid non-genomic anti-inflammatory and negative-feedback actions of glucocorticoids. Captures the fast arm of cortisol signalling that receptor-transcription models miss.
The second CRH receptor, preferentially bound by urocortins and generally opposing CRHR1 by supporting stress recovery rather than initiation. Represents the off-switch arm of CRH signalling.
Melanocortin receptor accessory protein, required to traffic MC2R to the cell surface and confer ACTH responsiveness. MC2R is non-functional without it, so the two must be read together.
Prohormone convertase 1/3, performing the cleavage of POMC to ACTH. Without it the precursor is made but the active hormone is not, so it is a rate-limiting post-translational step.
Co-chaperone promoting receptor degradation and inhibiting its transcriptional activity, acting as a negative regulator of glucocorticoid signalling. The disposal arm of the chaperone complex.
The partner co-chaperone FKBP52, which increases receptor affinity and promotes nuclear translocation, opposing FKBP5. The FKBP4 to FKBP5 ratio, not either alone, sets receptor sensitivity.
Corticosteroid binding globulin, carrying roughly 90 percent of circulating cortisol and determining the free fraction available to tissues. Sets the bioavailability of the entire axis output.
HOP, the adaptor handing the unliganded glucocorticoid receptor from HSP70 to HSP90 during maturation. A required assembly step for a receptor competent to bind cortisol.
Urocortin 2, a selective CRHR2 agonist involved in the delayed, recovery-phase component of the stress response. Methylation here bears on how quickly the axis returns to baseline.

Cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase, the obligatory electron donor for CYP17A1, CYP21A2 and CYP19A1. A single cofactor gene whose methylation could shift several steroidogenic steps at once.
Low-density lipoprotein receptor importing circulating cholesterol; steroidogenic cells prefer this route to de novo synthesis. The main substrate supply line in adrenal and gonadal tissue.

gene_name: cytochrome P450 family 1 subfamily A member 1
gene_function: Hydroxylates oestradiol to the relatively benign 2-hydroxy catechol and is induced by aryl hydrocarbons in tobacco smoke. Connects environmental exposure to oestrogen metabolism.

5-alpha-reductase type 2, the prostate and genital isoform responsible for male external differentiation; its deficiency causes 46,XY undervirilisation. The developmentally decisive isoform of the pair.
Performs the reverse oxidation, inactivating oestradiol to oestrone and testosterone to androstenedione. The HSD17B1 to HSD17B2 balance sets local active hormone concentration.
Better characterised as the ferritinophagy receptor delivering ferritin for degradation, with a secondary androgen receptor coactivator role. Links iron handling to androgen signalling.
Pioneer factor collaborating with FOXA1 to license androgen receptor binding, acting upstream of receptor recruitment. Part of the chromatin-accessibility layer of steroid signalling.
Sex hormone binding globulin, carrying testosterone and oestradiol in plasma and determining the free, bioavailable fraction. Total hormone levels are uninterpretable without it.

gene_function: Aromatase, converting androgens to oestrogens and so setting the local oestrogen-to-androgen ratio in brain, adipose and placenta. The most important switch in sex-steroid balance, and heavily promoter-regulated in a tissue-specific way.

gene_function: Directs oestradiol instead to the 4-hydroxy catechol, which is redox-active and DNA-damaging. The CYP1A1 to CYP1B1 ratio determines whether oestrogen metabolism is benign or genotoxic.

Androgen-regulated serine protease, best known for its prostate cancer fusion and as the SARS-CoV-2 entry protease. Its androgen responsiveness is the proposed basis for sex differences in COVID-19 severity.

Progesterone receptor, itself oestrogen-induced, governing uterine function, lactational readiness and progesterone's effects on mood. Its two isoforms arise from distinct promoters, so promoter methylation changes which isoform predominates.
Prostate-specific antigen, a canonical androgen receptor target and the standard readout that androgen signalling has occurred. A reporter rather than a regulator.
Glucuronidates androgens and oestrogens for excretion, one of the main terminal clearance routes. Determines how long a steroid signal persists.
3-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase inactivating DHT to androstanediol and generating allopregnanolone. Sits at the junction of androgen clearance and neurosteroid production.

G protein-coupled oestrogen receptor mediating rapid, non-genomic oestradiol signalling through cAMP and calcium. Captures the fast arm of oestrogen action on a timescale transcriptional receptors cannot explain.
Prostate-specific homeobox factor that partners the androgen receptor and reprogrammes its binding sites. Determines the tissue identity of the androgen response.
Converts oestrone to the far more potent oestradiol, mainly in placenta and granulosa cells. The activating step of the oestrogen branch.
Sulfonates DHEA to DHEA-S, the most abundant circulating steroid and a reservoir for peripheral androgen and oestrogen synthesis. Controls the size of the steroid precursor pool.
SRC-2, a coactivator with a tissue profile distinct from NCOA1 and a strong role in metabolic and reproductive tissue. Determines which target genes a given receptor actually activates.
17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 5, generating testosterone from androstenedione in peripheral tissue independently of the gonads. The main route to extragonadal androgen.
The liver-specific family member, dominating hepatic bile acid and steroid reduction. Its methylation bears on systemic steroid clearance rather than on local tissue action.

Oestrogen receptor beta, often opposing ESR1 and enriched in hypothalamus, hippocampus and amygdala. Generally linked to the anxiolytic and social effects of oestradiol rather than to reproductive ones.

Pioneer factor that opens compacted chromatin so androgen and oestrogen receptors can reach their response elements. Its binding is strongly methylation-sensitive, making it a direct route from DNA methylation to hormone responsiveness.
The testicular enzyme converting androstenedione to testosterone; deficiency causes 46,XY disorders of sex development. The final activating step of testicular androgen synthesis.
Oxidative enzyme with 3-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity that back-converts androstanediol to DHT, providing an alternative androgen route. Relevant where classical synthesis is limited.

Gi-coupled receptor present in human cortex and hippocampus but absent in rodents, and therefore poorly characterised. Its absence from animal models is itself the argument for measuring it in humans.

Gq-coupled receptor mediating cardiac valve growth, the basis of fenfluramine withdrawal; a stop-codon variant segregates with severe impulsivity in a Finnish pedigree. Peripheral toxicity and behaviour in one gene.

Orexin receptor 1, selective for orexin A and mediating arousal, reward and stress responses. The motivationally weighted receptor of the pair.

Paralogue with far lower catalytic activity and a restricted immune distribution, acting mainly in B cell tolerance. Present in the pathway but unlikely to drive flux.
Kynurenine aminotransferase III, the third kynurenic acid-producing enzyme, mitochondrially localised. Completes the protective branch.
Kynurenine aminotransferase II, the main producer of kynurenic acid, an NMDA and alpha7 nicotinic antagonist. The neuroprotective branch, and elevated in schizophrenia.

EAAT1 or GLAST, the astrocytic transporter dominant in cerebellum and during development. Complements SLC1A2 regionally.

gene_name: glutamate ionotropic receptor NMDA type subunit 2B

Group I receptor physically coupled to NMDA receptors through HOMER1 and SHANK, and a central node in fragile X and autism models. The most behaviourally implicated metabotropic receptor.
Retina-specific receptor mediating the ON bipolar cell response to light. Included for family completeness; not expected to be informative in saliva or blood.
PSD-95, the principal postsynaptic density scaffold anchoring NMDA receptors and coupling them to NOS1. The organising centre of the excitatory synapse.

EAAT3, the neuronal glutamate transporter, also implicated in obsessive-compulsive disorder. Neuronal rather than the bulk glial uptake route.
SAP97, scaffolding protein trafficking AMPA receptors and organising both sides of the synapse. Determines receptor delivery rather than receptor function.

Scaffold linking GRM5 to IP3 receptors and internal calcium stores; its short isoform Homer1a is an immediate-early gene that uncouples the complex during activity. Structural and activity-dependent at one locus.

gene_function: Beta subunit contributing to receptor assembly with a distinct regional profile, part of the chromosome 4p cluster. An assembly partner rather than a pharmacological determinant.

gene_name: gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit alpha3
caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: X-linked alpha subunit prominent in early development and in monoaminergic nuclei, later largely replaced by GABRA1. Its X-linkage requires within-sex analysis.

gene_name: gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit alpha4
gene_function: Benzodiazepine-insensitive subunit forming extrasynaptic receptors with delta and mediating tonic inhibition. A different mode of inhibition, not simply a different strength.

gene_name: gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit gamma2
gene_function: The gamma subunit required for benzodiazepine binding; without it the receptor functions but is benzodiazepine-insensitive. Mutations cause febrile seizures and epilepsy.
GAD67, producing the bulk of cytoplasmic GABA and setting the overall size of the GABA pool. Its reduction in prefrontal interneurons is one of the most replicated schizophrenia post-mortem findings.
GAD65, vesicle-associated and synthesising GABA on demand for phasic release. Supplies release-ready transmitter where GAD1 supplies the standing pool.
NKCC1, importing chloride and keeping intracellular chloride high in immature neurons, which makes GABA depolarising rather than inhibitory. One half of the developmental polarity switch.

gene_name: gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit alpha2
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Alpha subunit mediating anxiolysis without sedation, and one of the most replicated alcohol dependence loci. Separates the therapeutic from the sedating actions of benzodiazepines.

gene_name: gamma-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit beta2
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: The most widely expressed beta subunit, repeatedly associated with schizophrenia. Among the more consistently implicated GABA genes.
Glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor, the principal survival factor for midbrain dopamine neurons. The main trophic link between this system and dopamine.

caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: Synaptophysin, the most abundant synaptic vesicle protein and the standard quantitative marker of synapse density. A structural readout rather than a regulator.

caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: Synapsin I, tethering vesicles to the actin cytoskeleton and releasing them on phosphorylation, so it sets the size of the reserve pool. X-linked, and its mutation causes epilepsy with autism.

gene_name: nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1
gene_function: NUR77, an immediate-early nuclear receptor mediating activity-dependent synapse remodelling and dendritic distribution. Bridges the immediate-early and nuclear receptor families.
CREB-regulated transcription coactivator, translocating to the nucleus only on coincident calcium and cAMP signals. The molecular coincidence detector upstream of CREB1.
TrkB, the BDNF receptor; its truncated isoform acts as a dominant-negative sink. Which isoform predominates determines whether BDNF signals at all.

Brain-derived neurotrophic factor, the principal activity-dependent mediator of synaptic growth and survival, and the most studied gene in behavioural epigenetics after NR3C1. Promoter IV methylation is the canonical readout of early adversity, from Roth and Sweatt onward.
TrkA, the NGF receptor; loss of function causes congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis. Demonstrates how completely peripheral sensation depends on this pathway.
Immediate-early gene whose mRNA is transported to activated synapses and which drives AMPA receptor endocytosis. It encodes synapse-specific weakening, so the plasticity it supports is subtractive.
KROX20, an immediate-early gene also essential for hindbrain segmentation and Schwann cell myelination. Its developmental and activity-dependent roles are difficult to separate.
Immediate-early gene downstream of neurotrophin signalling and repeatedly associated with schizophrenia. Links activity-dependent transcription to psychiatric risk.

The only immediate-early gene induced selectively by neuronal activity rather than by any depolarising stimulus, and the specific regulator of inhibitory synapse formation. Uniquely activity-specific and inhibition-directed.
TrkC, the NT-3 receptor, which doubles as a synaptic adhesion molecule partnering PTPRS. Structural as well as trophic.
The GDNF receptor tyrosine kinase, also required for enteric nervous system development; its mutation causes Hirschsprung disease. A broader developmental role than its neurotrophic one.

gene_name: Fos proto-oncogene, AP-1 transcription factor subunit
gene_function: The canonical immediate-early gene, dimerising with JUN to form AP-1 and serving as the standard histological marker of neuronal activation. A transcriptional readout of recent activity.
Zinc finger immediate-early transcription factor coupling neuronal activity to lasting transcriptional change. Among the most widely used markers of recent neural activation.
Nerve growth factor, supporting cholinergic and sympathetic neuron survival centrally and mediating inflammatory pain sensitisation peripherally. Trophic in one compartment, nociceptive in the other.

gene_name: Jun proto-oncogene, AP-1 transcription factor subunit
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: The AP-1 partner of FOS, also acting in stress-activated signalling and apoptosis. Its dimer partner determines whether the output is growth or death.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Neurosecretory peptide precursor induced by BDNF and mediating part of its antidepressant-like effect. A downstream effector rather than a parallel factor.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Neurotrophin 3, acting mainly during development on proprioceptive and cortical neurons. More developmental than activity-dependent.
The Gs alpha subunit, an imprinted locus with complex tissue-specific parental expression whose disruption causes pseudohypoparathyroidism. Belongs equally to this system and to imprinted genes.
Phosphodiesterase 4D, the principal cAMP-degrading enzyme in brain and the target of rolipram, also associated with memory and stroke risk. Sets how long a cAMP signal persists.
G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2, phosphorylating agonist-occupied receptors to begin desensitisation. The first step in switching a receptor off.
Cyclase enriched in olfactory neurons and hypothalamus, with common variants strongly associated with obesity. Links this system to metabolic programming.

gene_name: protein kinase cAMP-activated catalytic subunit beta
gene_function: Second PKA catalytic subunit with a distinct tissue distribution and partial redundancy with PRKACA. Determines local rather than global PKA capacity.

gene_name: protein kinase cAMP-activated catalytic subunit alpha
gene_function: The main catalytic subunit of protein kinase A, the principal effector of every cAMP signal. The common endpoint of Gs-coupled receptor signalling.
Broadly expressed cyclase inhibited rather than stimulated by calcium, so it behaves opposite to ADCY1. Provides the calcium-suppressed arm of cAMP control.
The transcription factor at which cAMP, calcium and neurotrophin signalling converge, and the gateway to long-term memory. The transcriptional endpoint of most of this system.

gene_name: protein kinase cAMP-dependent type I regulatory subunit alpha
gene_function: The regulatory subunit holding PKA inactive until cAMP binds; its loss causes Carney complex through constitutive PKA activity. The actual cAMP sensor of the holoenzyme.
Calcium/calmodulin-stimulated adenylyl cyclase, the isoform making cAMP production conditional on prior calcium influx. A coincidence detector joining the calcium and cAMP arms.
Adenylyl cyclase stimulated by G protein beta-gamma subunits, with a robust bipolar disorder GWAS association. One of the more psychiatrically implicated cyclases.
Beta-arrestin 1, terminating G protein signalling and simultaneously initiating a separate arrestin-dependent cascade. Desensitisation and signalling in one molecule.
Beta-arrestin 2, mediating opioid receptor internalisation and implicated in separating analgesia from respiratory depression. The conceptual basis of biased agonist drug design.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Striatum-enriched cyclase whose mutations cause paroxysmal dyskinesia; the main cAMP source downstream of D1 and A2A receptors. Where dopamine and adenosine signals converge.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: AKAP79/150, anchoring PKA, PKC and calcineurin at the postsynaptic membrane so they act on defined targets. Converts a diffusible messenger into a local signal.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: mAKAP, anchoring PKA and phosphodiesterases at the nuclear envelope and sarcoplasmic reticulum. Provides compartmentalised cAMP control in heart and neurons.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Receptor kinase with a substrate preference distinct from GRK2 and a bias towards arrestin-mediated rather than G protein signalling. Determines which downstream pathway persists after desensitisation.

caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: Methyl-CpG binding protein that reads methylated DNA and recruits repressors; its mutation causes Rett syndrome. X-linked, so its CpGs are subject to X-inactivation and must be analysed within sex.
G9a, the main H3K9 dimethyltransferase producing facultative heterochromatin and required for cocaine-induced plasticity. The principal enzyme of activity-dependent silencing.
De novo methyltransferase acting mainly at pericentromeric satellite repeats in early embryogenesis; its mutation causes ICF syndrome. More embryonic and repeat-directed than DNMT3A.
CBP, the p300 paralogue whose haploinsufficiency causes Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome with intellectual disability. Demonstrates that acetyltransferase dosage is behaviourally consequential.

De novo methyltransferase establishing new methylation during development and in postmitotic neurons, where it mediates experience-dependent change. The enzyme most likely responsible for the effects this project is looking for.
MLL1, depositing activating H3K4 methylation at promoters; its mutation causes Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome. The activating counterpart to the Polycomb system.

gene_name: ubiquitin like with PHD and ring finger domains 1
gene_function: Reads hemimethylated DNA and recruits DNMT1 to it, making maintenance methylation possible. Without it DNMT1 cannot locate its substrate.

gene_name: enhancer of zeste 2 polycomb repressive complex 2 subunit
gene_function: Catalytic subunit of Polycomb repressive complex 2, depositing H3K27me3 to keep developmental genes switched off. The main mechanism holding alternative cell fates closed.

gene_name: SET domain bifurcated histone lysine methyltransferase 1
gene_function: H3K9 trimethyltransferase silencing endogenous retroviruses and imprinted loci. Guards the repetitive and imprinted compartments of the genome.
p300 histone acetyltransferase, the coactivator recruited by CREB1 and by nuclear receptors to open chromatin. Where signalling converges on histone acetylation.
Glycosylase repairing T:G mismatches at methylated CpG sites, the main defence against deamination-driven CpG loss. Explains why CpG dinucleotides are depleted genome-wide.
NAD+-dependent deacetylase coupling metabolic state to chromatin, and through NAD+ availability to the kynurenine pathway. Where cellular energy status becomes an epigenetic signal.

The maintenance methyltransferase copying methylation onto the daughter strand at replication, preserving patterns rather than creating them. Every measurement in this dataset depends on its fidelity.
Class IIa deacetylase shuttling between nucleus and cytoplasm under calcium control, so its activity is directly activity-dependent. Signal-responsive rather than constitutive.
The TET enzyme of the zygote and of postmitotic neurons, responsible for paternal genome demethylation after fertilisation. The developmentally decisive family member.
Class IIa deacetylase whose nuclear export is regulated by chronic stress and antidepressant exposure in the nucleus accumbens. A direct chromatin substrate of chronic stress.
NuRD component that, unusually for the family, cannot bind methylated DNA itself but is required for complex integrity. Structural rather than a reader.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Catalytically inactive cofactor stimulating DNMT3A and DNMT3B, and essential for germline imprint establishment. Regulatory rather than enzymatic, and the direct link to imprinting.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Histone deacetylase whose neuronal overexpression suppresses memory and whose inhibition restores it. The best-characterised chromatin link to learning.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Methyl-binding protein linking DNA methylation to H3K9 methylation and stable silencing; its loss impairs adult neurogenesis. Couples the two main repressive marks.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Methyl-binding component of the NuRD complex, coupling methylation to chromatin remodelling and deacetylation. The most direct route from a methyl mark to a closed chromatin state.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: TET enzyme dominant in haematopoietic cells and the most commonly mutated gene in clonal haematopoiesis. Directly relevant to any blood-derived methylation measurement in older participants.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Dioxygenase oxidising 5-methylcytosine to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, the first step of active demethylation. Note that bisulfite arrays cannot distinguish 5mC from 5hmC, so its product is invisible to this assay.

Neuronatin, paternally expressed and involved in calcium signalling and neurodevelopment, and among the most methylation-variable imprinted loci. Its variability makes it a sensitive detector but also a noisy one.
PEG1, paternally expressed and involved in mesoderm growth and maternal behaviour; its loss in mice produces deficient maternal care. A rare imprinted gene with a direct parenting phenotype.

Paternally expressed fetal growth factor whose imprinting control region is the classic case of environmentally sensitive imprinting; the Dutch Hunger Winter cohort showed persistent hypomethylation six decades after prenatal famine. The strongest precedent that a prenatal exposure can leave a lifelong methylation mark.
Paternally expressed antisense RNA silencing a cluster of maternally expressed genes across roughly one megabase. Demonstrates imprinting acting in trans across an entire domain.
ZAC1, paternally expressed and the hub of a network of co-regulated imprinted genes controlling fetal growth. Its loss of imprinting causes transient neonatal diabetes.
Maternally expressed non-coding RNA at the DLK1-DIO3 locus, regulating a large cluster of microRNAs. One of the few imprinted loci with clear postnatal brain function.
Paternally expressed zinc finger gene required for maternal nurturing and milk letdown, acting partly through oxytocin neuron number. Directly connects the imprinting and oxytocin systems.

Paternally expressed gene in the Prader-Willi region acting as a brake on puberty; its loss of function is the commonest known cause of central precocious puberty. Connects imprinting to HPG axis timing.

Paternally expressed gene in the 15q11-13 Prader-Willi region whose imprinting centre controls the whole domain; its methylation is the diagnostic test for Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes. The best-characterised imprinting centre in humans.

Necdin, paternally expressed in the same Prader-Willi region, promoting neuronal differentiation and required for normal oxytocin neuron development. A second link between imprinting and the oxytocin system.
Paternally expressed Notch ligand regulating adipogenesis and neurogenesis, reciprocal to MEG3 at the same locus. The protein-coding half of that imprinted pair.
Retrotransposon-derived paternally expressed gene essential for placental formation; its loss is embryonic lethal. Illustrates how a domesticated transposon became developmentally indispensable.

usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: Maternally expressed non-coding RNA reciprocally imprinted with IGF2 and sharing its control region. Loss of imprinting here causes Beckwith-Wiedemann and Silver-Russell syndromes, so the locus is dosage-critical.
Reduced folate carrier, the main route for folate uptake into cells. Determines intracellular folate availability regardless of dietary intake.
Transcobalamin 2, carrying vitamin B12 in plasma and delivering it into cells. B12 delivery, not circulating B12 level, is what limits MTR activity.
Betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase, a folate-independent route to remethylate homocysteine using betaine derived from choline. The backup methyl supply when folate is limiting.
Methionine synthase reductase, reactivating MTR after its cofactor oxidises. Without this recycling, MTR is inactivated after a limited number of turnovers.
Folate receptor alpha, a high-affinity uptake route critical at the placenta and choroid plexus; autoantibodies against it cause cerebral folate deficiency. The barrier-crossing transporter.

Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase, generating the methyl donor form of folate; the common C677T variant cuts activity by up to 70 percent and raises homocysteine. The single most important genetic determinant of methyl group supply.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase, clearing SAH, a potent inhibitor of every methyltransferase including DNMT1 and DNMT3A. The SAM to SAH ratio this enzyme sets is the direct biochemical determinant of methylation capacity.

usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: Cystathionine beta-synthase, diverting homocysteine into transsulfuration towards glutathione instead of remethylation. The branch point between methylation capacity and antioxidant capacity.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Methionine synthase, transferring the methyl group from folate to homocysteine to make methionine, and requiring vitamin B12. The junction of the folate and B12 cycles.
Arylalkylamine N-acetyltransferase, the rate-limiting and sharply rhythmic enzyme of melatonin synthesis. Its activity varies more than tenfold across the day, making it the clock's output amplifier.
Casein kinase 1 epsilon, phosphorylating PER proteins to target them for degradation and thereby setting period length. Mutation here produces the short-period tau phenotype.
MT2 melatonin receptor, mediating circadian phase shifting rather than sedation, and carrying one of the strongest type 2 diabetes GWAS variants. Phase-shifting and metabolic in one gene.
Period 3, carrying a variable number tandem repeat associated with morningness and sleep homeostasis. Probes here may be affected by the repeat, so interpret with care.
Cryptochrome 2, contributing to repression with a temporal profile distinct from CRY1. Fine-tunes the period rather than setting it.

gene_name: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group D member 1
gene_function: REV-ERB alpha, forming a second interlocking loop by repressing ARNTL, and also a heme sensor linking metabolism to the clock. Where metabolic state feeds back on timing.
Retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor alpha, activating ARNTL in opposition to NR1D1 and separately implicated in autism. Belongs to both the circadian and neurodevelopmental literatures.

caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: Acetylserotonin O-methyltransferase, the final enzyme converting N-acetylserotonin to melatonin. It lies in the pseudoautosomal region, so it escapes X-inactivation and is present in two active copies in both sexes.
Transcription factor dimerising with ARNTL to drive the positive limb of the circadian loop, and itself a histone acetyltransferase. Directly couples circadian timing to chromatin state.
Cryptochrome 1, the stronger repressor of the negative limb; a splice variant causes delayed sleep phase disorder. The dominant partner of the PER-CRY complex.
MT1 melatonin receptor, mediating the acute sleep-promoting and SCN-inhibiting effects of melatonin. The sedating arm of melatonin action.
Period 2, the repressor whose mutation causes familial advanced sleep phase syndrome. The clearest single-gene determinant of human chronotype.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: BMAL1, the obligate CLOCK partner and the only clock gene whose single deletion abolishes circadian rhythmicity entirely. The non-redundant core of the oscillator.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Period 1, a negative-limb repressor that is also directly glucocorticoid-inducible, making it the main entry point for cortisol into the clock. Where the HPA axis meets circadian timing.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Clock-associated protein whose principal mammalian role is in replication fork protection and the DNA damage response. More a genome stability gene than a core oscillator component in humans.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DP alpha 1
gene_function: Class II alpha chain of the DP heterodimer, less polymorphic than DR or DQ, presenting extracellular peptides to CD4 T cells. The stable half of the DP pair.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DP beta 1
gene_function: The DP beta chain, associated with hepatitis B vaccine response and beryllium sensitivity. The polymorphic half of the DP dimer.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DM beta
gene_function: Class II accessory molecule catalysing peptide exchange in the endosome so high-affinity peptides are loaded. Determines the quality of what is presented, not whether presentation happens.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DP beta 2 (pseudogene)
gene_function: Pseudogene at the DP locus retaining regulatory sequence but producing no protein. Methylation here indexes local chromatin state rather than gene function.
Sensor forming the inflammasome that cleaves pro-IL-1beta into its active form, activated by cellular stress and metabolic danger signals. The step at which stress becomes inflammation.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DQ beta 2
gene_function: The beta chain partner of HLA-DQA2, expressed at low levels with an incompletely defined role. Included for locus completeness.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, F
gene_function: Non-classical class I molecule with roles in NK regulation and at the maternal-fetal interface. Its function remains incompletely resolved.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, L (pseudogene)
gene_function: Class I pseudogene, transcribed at low levels with no known function. A regional rather than a functional signal.

The membrane IL-6 receptor giving classical, largely regenerative signalling; its soluble form instead drives pro-inflammatory trans-signalling. Which form predominates determines the direction of the IL-6 effect.

Pattern recognition receptor for bacterial lipopolysaccharide and for endogenous danger signals released by tissue stress. The main route by which sterile psychological stress can engage innate immunity.
Antisense transcript regulating HLA-F expression in cis. Indexes regulation of the locus rather than the molecule.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, G
gene_function: Non-classical class I molecule expressed by extravillous trophoblast to induce maternal immune tolerance of the fetus. The central molecule of maternal-fetal tolerance, and directly relevant to a pregnancy cohort.
The principal anti-inflammatory cytokine, restraining and terminating the inflammatory response. The IL-6 to IL-10 balance is more informative than either measured alone.
Receptor subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23; its deficiency causes mycobacterial susceptibility. The common receptor half of both pathways.
Inflammasome-processed cytokine driving interferon gamma production, sharing activation machinery with IL1B but with a distinct downstream profile. The Th1-directing arm of inflammasome output.
Tumour necrosis factor, a central pro-inflammatory cytokine located inside the MHC region and a core CTRA gene. Its MHC position means methylation here may partly reflect haplotype.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, B
gene_function: Highly polymorphic class I molecule presenting intracellular peptides to CD8 T cells. Extreme sequence polymorphism means probe hybridisation itself varies by haplotype, so interpret with caution.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DO beta
gene_function: The beta chain partner of HLA-DOA, completing the HLA-DM inhibitory complex. Non-functional without its partner.
Antisense transcript regulating IL12A expression in cis. Indexes regulation of the locus rather than the cytokine.
The p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23, so it feeds two different T helper programmes. A shared subunit whose regulation affects both Th1 and Th17 responses.

Pleiotropic cytokine that is pro- or anti-inflammatory depending on whether it signals classically or by trans-signalling, and the most measured marker in psychoneuroimmunology. Its ambiguity is intrinsic, not a measurement problem.
MCP-1, recruiting monocytes into tissue and mediating the monocyte trafficking that underlies stress-induced inflammation. The chemotactic arm of the CTRA.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, C
gene_function: Class I molecule presenting peptides to CD8 T cells and the main ligand for killer immunoglobulin receptors on NK cells. Bridges adaptive and innate recognition.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DO alpha
gene_function: Modulator of HLA-DM activity in B cells and thymic epithelium, biasing which peptides are selected. A regulator of the regulator.
The IL-12-specific receptor subunit conferring Th1 selectivity. What distinguishes an IL-12 from an IL-23 response at the receptor.
gp130, the shared signal transducer for IL-6 and related cytokines and the obligatory partner for all IL-6 signalling. A single gene mediating an entire cytokine family.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DQ alpha 2
gene_function: Class II alpha chain of the less-studied DQ2 pair, expressed mainly in Langerhans cells. Distinct in expression pattern from the classical HLA-DQA1.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DR alpha
gene_function: The invariant class II alpha chain, essentially monomorphic and pairing with any DR beta chain. Its constancy makes it the cleanest quantitative index of class II expression on the array.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DR beta 1
gene_function: The most polymorphic class II gene and the site of the strongest genetic associations with autoimmune disease. Haplotype variation is extreme, so treat probe signal here cautiously.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DR beta 9 (pseudogene)
gene_function: Class II pseudogene fragment retained in the DR region. A haplotype and chromatin marker rather than a functional gene.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, E
gene_function: Non-classical, minimally polymorphic class I molecule presenting leader peptides to NK cells as evidence that class I synthesis is intact. A self-integrity check rather than an antigen presenter.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, H (pseudogene)
gene_function: Class I pseudogene retaining promoter and regulatory sequence but producing no protein. Useful as a regional chromatin readout, not as a functional gene.

Interleukin 1 beta, the prototypical pro-inflammatory cytokine released after inflammasome activation and a core CTRA response-to-adversity gene. Among the most consistently upregulated transcripts under chronic social threat.
Antisense long non-coding RNA at the IL6R locus, regulating receptor expression in cis. Probes here index regulation of IL6R rather than IL6R itself.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DR beta 6 (pseudogene)
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Class II pseudogene present only on DR1, DR2 and DR10 haplotypes, disrupted by a retroviral insertion. Its very presence is haplotype-dependent.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, J (pseudogene)
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Class I pseudogene within the MHC, transcribed but never translated into a functional molecule. Interpret as a marker of the regulatory landscape.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, K (pseudogene)
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Class I pseudogene in the MHC region with no protein product. Included because the array covers it and it reports on local chromatin.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Adhesion molecule enabling leukocytes to cross the endothelium into tissue, and elevated under chronic stress. The step converting circulating inflammation into tissue infiltration.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: The p35 subunit of IL-12, driving Th1 differentiation. Functional only when paired with IL12B, so its methylation must be read jointly with it.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: The transcription factor at which most inflammatory signals converge, and the proposed molecular substrate of the conserved transcriptional response to adversity. The hub of the CTRA model.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Complement component 4A, whose copy number drives microglial synaptic pruning and provides the mechanism behind the strongest schizophrenia GWAS signal. Probes here may reflect copy number as much as methylation.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: C-reactive protein, the acute phase protein synthesised by liver under IL-6 control and the standard clinical inflammation marker. A downstream readout rather than a driver.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class II, DR beta 5
usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: Beta chain present only on certain DR haplotypes, notably DR15, and absent entirely in many people. Probe signal partly indexes haplotype presence rather than methylation.

gene_name: major histocompatibility complex, class I, S (pseudogene)
usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: Class I pseudogene fragment in the MHC. Reports on chromatin state of the region rather than on any gene product.

usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: T cell receptor alpha constant region; its methylation and rearrangement status index alpha-beta T cell abundance. Effectively a cell composition marker, which matters given the EpiDISH deconvolution in this pipeline.

usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: T cell receptor delta constant region, marking the gamma-delta lineage, and deleted during alpha-beta commitment. Its retention indexes an unconventional T cell population.

usability: NOT ON ARRAY - no EPIC v2 probe exists
gene_function: T cell receptor gamma constant region 1, marking gamma-delta T cells, which are enriched at mucosal surfaces including oral mucosa. Directly relevant to saliva-derived samples.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: The second gamma constant region, used by a distinct gamma-delta subset. Complements TRGC1 as a lineage marker.

caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: X-linked neuroligin whose R451C mutation was among the first identified monogenic causes of autism. Its X-linkage requires within-sex analysis.
Neuregulin 1, signalling through ERBB4 to regulate myelination, interneuron development and NMDA receptor function. A historically central schizophrenia candidate gene.
Activity-dependent transcription factor driving synapse elimination; its haploinsufficiency causes intellectual disability with limited speech. The transcriptional controller of synaptic pruning.

Presynaptic adhesion molecule with thousands of splice isoforms, and one of the most robust copy number associations across autism and schizophrenia. Deletion here is an established psychiatric risk factor.

Transcription factor whose disruption causes a severe speech and language disorder in the KE family, the first gene implicated in human language. Acts by repressing a large downstream programme including CNTNAP2.
Neurexin family member contributing to presynaptic organisation with a distinct isoform repertoire. Less strongly implicated than NRXN1 but mechanistically parallel.
The inhibitory counterpart, localising exclusively to GABAergic synapses. With NLGN1 it sets the excitation-inhibition ratio structurally.
Neurexin implicated in addiction and obesity as well as synaptic organisation. The family member with the clearest non-psychiatric associations.

gene_name: activator of transcription and developmental regulator AUTS2
gene_function: Neurodevelopmental regulator of neurite outgrowth and a Polycomb-associated transcriptional regulator, lying in a region of accelerated human evolution. Both a synaptic and a chromatin gene.

CASPR2, a neurexin superfamily member regulating potassium channel clustering and cortical development; recessive mutations cause cortical dysplasia with focal epilepsy. Also a FOXP2 target, which links it to language.
Postsynaptic adhesion molecule specifying excitatory synapses by binding presynaptic neurexins. Determines synapse type rather than synapse number.

Reelin, guiding neuronal migration during cortical layering and modulating adult plasticity; its promoter hypermethylation is a long-standing schizophrenia finding. One of the earliest psychiatric methylation candidates.

Dysbindin, regulating vesicular trafficking and glutamate release; reduced prefrontal expression in schizophrenia is well documented despite weak GWAS support. A case where expression evidence outran genetic evidence.

Alpha-7 nicotinic receptor mediating sensory gating, with a partial duplication that complicates both genotyping and probe interpretation. The molecular basis of the P50 gating deficit in schizophrenia.
The NRG1 receptor, concentrated on parvalbumin interneurons where it regulates inhibitory tone. Where the neuregulin signal is actually received.

caution: X-linked: X-inactivation makes female values a two-allele average - analyse within sex or model sex explicitly
gene_function: X-linked neuroligin with the strongest autism association in the family, and partially escaping X-inactivation. Both its linkage and its partial escape complicate methylation interpretation.
Deiodinase 2, generating T3 locally within brain and pituitary so that tissue T3 is regulated independently of blood levels. The reason serum thyroid measures understate brain exposure.
Deiodinase 3, inactivating thyroid hormone and highly expressed in placenta, where it shields the fetus from maternal T3. It also sits in the imprinted DLK1-MEG3 locus, belonging to both systems.

Thyroid hormone receptor alpha, dominant in brain, heart and bone and the principal mediator of thyroid effects on neurodevelopment. The receptor through which maternal thyroid status reaches the fetal brain.
The TSH receptor on thyroid follicular cells, driving hormone synthesis and the target of stimulating autoantibodies in Graves disease. The single relay from pituitary to thyroid.
Deiodinase 1, converting T4 to active T3 mainly in liver and kidney and contributing to the circulating T3 pool. The systemic activation route.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Thyroid hormone receptor beta, dominant in liver and in pituitary feedback; its mutation causes resistance to thyroid hormone. The receptor governing the axis's own set point.
Ghrelin, the only known circulating orexigenic hormone, rising before meals and also acting on reward and stress circuits. The hunger signal, with a secondary role in stress coping.
The master transcriptional regulator of adipocyte differentiation and the target of thiazolidinediones. Determines how many fat cells form and how insulin-sensitive they are.

PGC-1 alpha, the coactivator driving mitochondrial biogenesis in response to exercise and cold; its promoter methylation responds to a single bout of acute exercise. One of the few loci with demonstrated short-term environmental methylation change in humans.
Melanocortin 3 receptor, regulating energy partitioning and, as recently shown, the timing of puberty in relation to nutritional state. Links this system to the HPG axis.
Cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript, an anorexigenic peptide co-expressed with POMC in hypothalamic neurons. Reinforces the satiety arm.

Leptin, secreted by adipose tissue in proportion to fat mass and signalling energy sufficiency to the hypothalamus. Its promoter methylation in cord blood is a leading marker of prenatal metabolic programming.
Insulin-like growth factor 1, the principal mediator of growth hormone action and a determinant of fetal and postnatal growth. Directly relevant to the birth weight phenotypes in this cohort.
Insulin, whose variable number tandem repeat is imprinted and associated with birth weight and type 1 diabetes. Metabolic and imprinted at once.
Agouti-related peptide, an inverse agonist at MC4R that actively drives feeding, opposing alpha-MSH. The orexigenic half of the melanocortin balance.
The IGF-1 receptor mediating growth and, in model organisms, extending lifespan when signalling is reduced. Links growth programming to ageing.

Melanocortin 4 receptor, the downstream effector of POMC-derived alpha-MSH and the commonest monogenic cause of obesity. Also the point at which the POMC precursor serves appetite rather than the HPA axis.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: The strongest common obesity locus, acting through long-range regulation of IRX3 and IRX5 rather than on itself, and separately an m6A RNA demethylase. Its methylation is not simply an obesity readout.

usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: The leptin receptor; signalling defects here produce leptin resistance, in which high leptin fails to suppress appetite. Explains why obesity coexists with elevated leptin.

gene_name: four and a half LIM domains 2
gene_function: Four and a half LIM domains 2, a transcriptional cofactor whose promoter methylation increases robustly with age across tissues. A standard component of forensic age prediction panels.
Helicase resolving telomeric secondary structures during replication; its mutation causes Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome, a severe telomere biology disorder. Required to replicate the telomere at all.

The catalytic subunit of telomerase, rate-limiting for telomere maintenance; its promoter is the most frequently mutated non-coding region in cancer. Methylation here has a paradoxical positive relationship with expression.
Aspartoacylase, whose deficiency causes Canavan disease and whose promoter methylation is a well-validated age marker. Its clock utility is unrelated to its metabolic function.
Adaptor in ectodysplasin signalling whose methylation decreases with age, giving a marker that moves opposite to most others. That directionality is itself what makes it useful in a panel.
Fatty acid elongase whose promoter shows the strongest and most reproducible age-related hypermethylation of any locus in the human genome. The single best univariate methylation age predictor known.
Maternally imprinted transcription factor acting as a master regulator of adipose gene expression, and age-associated in its methylation. Imprinted and age-related simultaneously.
Protection of telomeres 1, binding the single-stranded overhang and regulating telomerase access. Its mutation causes familial melanoma and glioma through telomere lengthening.
TRF1, a shelterin component binding double-stranded telomeric DNA and negatively regulating telomere length. The main length-sensing brake.
TRF2, the shelterin component preventing the telomere end from being read as a double-strand break. Protects against end-to-end fusion rather than setting length.
Tripartite motif protein whose methylation is a consistent age marker and a component of several forensic age models. Included as a clock marker rather than for its immune function.
The mitochondrial manganese superoxide dismutase, handling superoxide at its main site of production. The most consequential antioxidant enzyme for mitochondrial integrity.
NRF2, the master transcription factor inducing the entire antioxidant response programme once oxidative stress is detected. Coordinate control of everything else in this system.

Quinone reductase performing two-electron reduction to avoid generating radical intermediates; a common null polymorphism is frequent in some populations. A detoxification enzyme with substantial genetic variation.
Catalase, decomposing hydrogen peroxide to water at extremely high turnover, mainly in peroxisomes. Handles bulk peroxide where GPX1 handles low concentrations.
Glutathione peroxidase 1, reducing hydrogen peroxide using glutathione and requiring selenium. Links selenium status to antioxidant capacity, as SELENON does for calcium handling.

Cytosolic copper-zinc superoxide dismutase, the first line of defence against cytosolic superoxide; its mutation causes familial ALS through toxic gain of function. Loss and gain of function here have entirely different consequences.

usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: Mitochondrial transcription factor A, packaging mitochondrial DNA and determining copy number. Mitochondrial DNA copy number is itself an increasingly used stress biomarker.

gene_name: cytochrome P450 family 2 subfamily D member 6 (gene/pseudogene)
usability: SINGLE PROBE - cannot support a gene-level claim
gene_function: Metabolises roughly a quarter of prescribed drugs including most antidepressants and antipsychotics, with copy number ranging from zero to more than ten. Probe signal here is heavily confounded by copy number, so interpret methylation with real caution.

gene_name: cytochrome P450 family 3 subfamily A member 4
usability: NO USABLE PROBE - all filtered out for low variance
gene_function: The single most important drug-metabolising enzyme, handling around half of all clinical drugs and strongly inducible by exposure. Its inducibility makes methylation here potentially exposure-responsive rather than merely constitutive.
